# Acute Heart Failure: Ward Protocol

Synthetic teaching text for tests, not clinical guidance. Edition 2023.

## Diagnosis

Acute heart failure is a rapid onset of symptoms and signs of congestion or hypoperfusion at rest. Dyspnoea, orthopnoea and raised jugular venous pressure are the bedside triad. BNP above 100 pg/mL supports the diagnosis.

## Treatment

Intravenous furosemide 40 mg is the starting dose for a patient not on diuretics. Reassess urine output at 6 hours. Add a thiazide when the response is poor after 24 hours.

- Nitrates reduce preload and are first line when systolic pressure is above 110 mmHg.
- Routine morphine eases dyspnoea and anxiety.
- Inotropes are for cardiogenic shock.

## Pitfalls

Do not give fluids for a low blood pressure that comes with congestion. Check potassium and renal function after every diuretic dose change.

## Numbers to remember

| Variable | Threshold |
| --- | --- |
| BNP | >100 pg/mL |
| Furosemide start | 40 mg IV |
| Urine sodium | <50 mmol/L at 6 h |

## Discharge

Arrange a clinic visit within 2 weeks of discharge and send the summary to the family doctor.
